trickyParts: The owner lock is pg_advisory_xact_lock(0x4F574E52, hashtext(kind:key)) and its read is a separate statement in the same batch: under READ COMMITTED a combined statement takes its snapshot before it waits and would miss a close committed meanwhile (TestACloseCommittedWhileAWriterWaitsOnTheOwnerLockIsRefused).

The write phase is one pipelined pgx batch; values a later statement needs (event seq, owner last_seq and updated_at, ask.opened's opened_event_id, reference stamps via currval, thread logins, review event_seq) are derived in SQL, with an equality test per derived value.
Reads that saw the transaction's own writes are resolved from the ledger (pending appends, versions, anchors, approvals, references, reviews): dispatch://INFRA-636/artifact/reads-after-writes-md.
The horizon's writer invariant holds: the queued owner row-lock statement carries pg_current_xact_id() before the event insert; an ownerless event queues its own pg_current_xact_id().

One horizon observation proves itself when its snapshot's in-progress list is empty and its xmax equals the observer's id; the argument is in events/horizon.go's header beside the xmax-hole case, with tests for a quiet instance, an open xid holder and the hole.

A settlement sends the same owner-lock statement as a PATCH, so the shutdown test tells the title change's backend from the settlement's by the settlement's own document advisory lock, which it holds before it asks for the owner lock.

awaitNoTransactionIDHolder could return before the issue create's search-term refresh began, or while its rebuild was in its read part; it now waits for search_term_totals' TEST row, which that refresh commits.
deviations: Scope widened per decision D5 to every transaction that held an id across document work or advice: settlement, edit-notice sweep, task-progress reconciliation, block-index backfill, decided-wording restoration, issue close and reopen.
Acceptance 1's check is the D6 threshold and acceptance 2's decisive metric the backend_xid hold (D7), both accepted by the architect.

To meet the frame bar this PR also changes INFRA-591's horizon cadence (immediate re-observation, eager notification read, self-proof) and the relay's coalescing window (25 ms to 2 ms), as the architect assigned on 2026-10-28.
Rollout: an earlier release's pod and this one's do not exclude each other's writes to one owner; serve this release at one pod with Recreate before adding pods (changelog fragment).
